clue.text: Flag lowered finally, miserable in retreat

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word lowered
something in retreat goes backwards, so the synonym for miserable is read in reverse

parts.note: miserable can mean poor, as in a poor showing

explanation.surface: A flag hauled down at last, a sorry sight as an army falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a noun for a banner but is the verb meaning to tire. 'in retreat' turns POOR into ROOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or sag with tiredness, the same sense as wilting or sagging.

clue.text: Son of Jacob nursing swelling, he is lumbered

indicators.note: nursing means holding something close, so the son's name wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve sons of Jacob in Genesis
a lump is a swelling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biblical son carrying a painful swelling is stuck with an unwanted burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lumbered' looks like 'burdened' but here means moved heavily; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To galumph is to move in a clumsy, heavy-footed way, which is to lumber along.

clue.text: Was substituted? Strange!

definitions.meaning: a player who is substituted walks off the pitch, read as two words
as an adjective, unconventional or odd, out of the mainstream

explanation.surface: A puzzled cry on seeing someone replaced unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the phrase into a verb and a noun: the player departed the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of left field is an American baseball idiom for unexpected or eccentric, hence strange.

clue.text: Romeo in bunk becoming surly

indicators.note: in places the letter for Romeo inside the word for nonsense

parts.note: bunk is nonsense, as is guff
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lover in a bed turning bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' suggests a bed but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruff manner is rough and unfriendly, much like a surly one.

clue.text: Sweet thing, remarkably genial wife filling in puzzle

indicators.note: filling in says the other pieces go inside the word for puzzle

parts.note: to puzzle someone is to baffle them

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of genial are arranged in a striking new way

explanation.surface: A charming wife completes a crossword, a sweet thing indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' turns GENIAL into ELGIAN, which with W fills BAFFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian waffle is a thick sweet batter cake, often eaten with cream or syrup.

clue.text: Anger, with one enjoying a carefree life cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: someone living the life of Riley has an easy, carefree time, so Riley is that person

explanation.surface: Fury at someone whose idle, easy existence is suddenly ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The life of Riley' is an English idiom for a comfortable, carefree life; 'cut short' drops its final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To rile someone is to annoy or irritate them, which is to make them angry.

clue.text: Stop company cutting funds for home protection

parts.note: to dam is to stop a flow

indicators.note: cutting means the abbreviation slices into the word for funds

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money or funds, as in a prize purse

explanation.surface: A firm's cuts halt the money set aside for household security.
explanation.walkthrough: A damp course is a waterproof layer laid in a house wall to stop moisture rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp-proof barrier built into walls guards a building against rising moisture.

clue.text: Sneaky blighter, I'm a con

indicators.note: sneaky suggests something underhand, so the letters are shifted round deceptively

explanation.surface: A villain confesses to being a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sneaky' rearranges BLIGHTER plus IM; 'blighter' is British slang for a rotter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thimblerig is the three-cups-and-a-pea sleight-of-hand swindle, a classic street trick.

clue.text: Reportedly cross, whimper

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for cross is said out loud

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone said to be angry ends up whining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is a noun: a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mewl is to cry feebly like a baby or kitten, a weak whimpering noise.

clue.text: Unexpected U-turn with date and deal complete

indicators.note: unexpected suggests things turning out differently, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A surprise reversal on a date and an agreement that is now finalised.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadulterated means pure or utter, as in unadulterated nonsense, which is total or complete.

clue.text: Fighter starts to box intelligently, presenting defence

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxer

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A boxer begins boxing cleverly, mounting a good guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence' looks like a boxer's guard but is a legal defence.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, offered in court as a defence against a charge.

clue.text: He wrote in earnest, even so, needlessly

indicators.note: in says the name is tucked inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A writer worked seriously but, even so, without any need.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Proscribe different tokens for cash

parts.note: to proscribe is to forbid or ban

indicators.note: different means the letters of tokens are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Banning various vouchers in exchange for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper money such as a twenty-pound note is cash in its most familiar form.

clue.text: Skimpy briefs a possible source of irritation when viewed from behind

indicators.note: viewing from behind means reading back to front

parts.note: a gnat bite can be an irritation

explanation.surface: Tiny underwear that might chafe, seen from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when viewed from behind' fits briefs neatly but reverses A GNAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanga is a brief style of bikini bottom or underpants with a thin strip at the sides.

clue.text: Planned debate

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to consider carefully or discuss

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means intentional; as a verb it means to weigh up or discuss.

clue.text: Festering cricket side

definitions.meaning: going bad or rotten, like food past its date
in cricket the ... side is the half of the field facing the batsman

explanation.definitionFit: Spoilt meat is said to be gone bad; cricket divides the field into the leg side and its opposite.

clue.text: Excessively complimentary review in flier

parts.note: a puff is an overly flattering write-up or plug

explanation.surface: A gushing write-up appears in a pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' looks like a leaflet but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The puffin is a seabird with a bright beak, so it is one kind of thing that flies.

clue.text: Fruit garden's odd parts fascinate

indicators.note: odd parts are the first, third and fifth letters of the word garden

parts.note: to engage someone is to hold their attention, to fascinate them

explanation.surface: Strange features of an orchard hold the attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in garden's is read as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a sweet green variety of plum, a tree fruit.

clue.text: Ancient region largely evacuated before help turned up

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, leaving only the outside letters
in a down entry turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: An old territory mostly emptied before assistance arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia was a kingdom of western Asia Minor, ruled by Croesus.

clue.text: Huge disappointment? That's the measure of computing

definitions.meaning: an enormous failure, a really big letdown
a unit of computer speed: a million floating-point operations per second

explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a failure, so a mega one is huge; in computing it is also a processing-speed unit.

clue.text: One must stay in under this

definitions.text: One must stay in under this

parts.words: One must stay in under this
parts.note: stay in looks like a night at home but is a legal confinement order

explanation.definitionFit: A detention order confining someone to their home means they must not go out.

clue.text: Bad pud

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses it for something worthless; a plum version is a steamed suet pudding.

clue.text: Very small place, one secured by girl

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the girl's name

parts.note: Lillian is a girl's name
to place something is to put it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tiny spot, with someone held fast by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very small place' tempts as a definition of the island itself, but 'place' is PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliput's inhabitants in Gulliver's Travels are six inches tall, so the word means tiny.

clue.text: Siren trouble girl raised as blooming deadly thing?

parts.note: a bell sounds an alarm, as a siren does
ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means written upwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A seductress, a troubled girl, brought up to be a fatal temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siren' and 'deadly' paint a femme fatale; 'blooming' points instead to a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade is a poisonous flowering plant whose berries can kill.

clue.text: Futile, to be blunt?

definitions.meaning: lacking a sharp tip, read as a whimsical second sense

explanation.definitionFit: A useless effort has no purpose; something blunt literally has no sharp end.

clue.text: Offering nothing in classical language, alumnus going first

indicators.note: going first puts the old boy at the front

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the language

parts.note: Latin was the language of ancient Rome
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Giving nothing in Latin class, a former pupil leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: OB is short for old boy, British term for a school's former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblation is a gift presented to God or a deity, a religious offering.

clue.text: Pirates at sea without a prayer?

indicators.note: at sea means muddled, so the letters of Pirates are jumbled
without means one letter a is left out of the jumble

explanation.surface: Buccaneers on the ocean with no hope at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a prayer' reads as an idiom for hopeless; 'prayer' is someone who prays.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric leads worship and prays on behalf of others, so is one who prays.

clue.text: Happy band, distressed

parts.note: up means cheerful, as in feeling up
a set is a group or band of people

explanation.surface: A cheerful group of musicians suddenly upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset is feeling troubled or unhappy, much the same as being distressed.

clue.text: Post or stick, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks whether the word is being heard spoken

parts.note: to jam is to get stuck

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone said post or stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright side piece of a door or window frame, a vertical post.

clue.text: Beginning to seem cool, crime

indicators.note: beginning to selects the first letter of seem

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: Crime starts to look stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wrongful act, an offence against moral or religious law.
